messages.author: 79b31c930c78e998
messages.subject: two-dimensional P-spline
parts:
Hi,

is it possible to include in an INLA model a two-dimensional P-spline term (numerical variables) like the 'pspline2dimrw1' of BayesX?

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] two-dimensional P-spline
parts:
On Wed, 2015-04-01 at 03:08 -0700, Donal Bisanzio wrote:
> Hi,
>
> is it possible to include in an INLA model a two-dimensional P-spline
> term (numerical variables) like the 'pspline2dimrw1' of BayesX?
>
>

we do not have an easy acccess to such interaction, and I agree that
this would be a nice feature. there is however, a general
interaction `tool', using SPDE's for Gaussian fields. you'll find
tutorials here

http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials

I hope this helps.

Best,

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] two-dimensional P-spline
parts:
The rw2d model is a more direct translation of the pspline2dimrw1 model, except it uses 2nd order difference penalties instead of first order differences:
http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/latent/rw2d-model.pdf

The spde alternative can be used in a way that allows 2nd order b-spline bases for a squared second order derivatives penalty model, but currently you'd need to use inla.mesh.1d() and inla.mesh.1d.fem() and kronecker() to construct a precision matrix to feed into a "generic0" model, as we don't have a wrapper function for this kind of model.
The "read this first" tutorial has a 1d example of a penalized spline model with 2nd order basis functions.

Finn
